claim: You do not need to enable or set up anything to view the past 90 days of account activity in the CloudTrail console or AWS CLI.
question: Do I need to set up CloudTrail to view my account activity?

values.display: nothing is required to begin viewing
up to the past 90 days of account activity

evidence.quote: No, nothing is required to begin viewing your account activity. You can visit the AWS CloudTrail console or AWS CLI and begin viewing up to the past 90 days of account activity.

claim: CloudTrail Event history shows results only for the current Region you are viewing, for the last 90 days, and its events are limited to management events that create, modify, and delete API calls and account activity.
question: Does the CloudTrail Event history show all account activity within my account?

values.display: current Region you are viewing for the last 90 days
limited to management events

evidence.quote: AWS CloudTrail will only show the results of the CloudTrail Event history for the current Region you are viewing for the last 90 days, and supports a range of AWS services . These events are limited to management events that create, modify, and delete API calls and account activity.

claim: For a complete record of account activity, including all management events, data events, and read-only activity, you must configure a CloudTrail trail.
question: What do I need for a complete record of account activity in CloudTrail?

values.display: must configure a CloudTrail trail
data events, and read-only activity

evidence.quote: For a complete record of account activity, including all management events, data events, and read-only activity, you must configure a CloudTrail trail.

claim: You can use the CloudTrail console or the CloudTrail API/CLI to view the past 90 days of account activity.
question: Can I use the lookup-events CLI command even if I don't have a trail configured?

values.display: CloudTrail API/CLI
past 90 days of account activity

evidence.quote: Yes, you can visit the CloudTrail console or use the CloudTrail API/CLI and begin viewing the past 90 days of account activity.

claim: There is no cost for viewing or searching account activity with CloudTrail Event History.
question: Is there any cost for CloudTrail Event History?

values.display: no cost for viewing or searching account activity
CloudTrail Event History

evidence.quote: There is no cost for viewing or searching account activity with CloudTrail Event History.

claim: You can stop logging or delete a trail, which also stops delivery of account activity to the S3 bucket and to CloudWatch Logs if configured. Account activity for the past 90 days is still collected and visible in the CloudTrail console and the AWS CLI.
question: Can I turn off CloudTrail Event History for my account?

values.display: stop logging or delete the trails
past 90 days will still be collected

evidence.quote: For any CloudTrail trails created, you can stop logging or delete the trails. This will also stop account activity delivery to the Amazon S3 bucket you designated as part of your trail configuration and delivery to CloudWatch Logs if configured. Account activity for the past 90 days will still be collected and visible within the CloudTrail console and through the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI).

claim: With direct delivery of CloudTrail events to CloudWatch, you can centrally manage event collection across your organization from the CloudWatch console without configuring individual trails, which reduces operational overhead.
question: What advantages does direct integration of CloudTrail and CloudWatch offer?

values.display: direct delivery of CloudTrail events to CloudWatch
without having to configure individual trails

evidence.quote: With direct delivery of CloudTrail events to CloudWatch, you gain several key advantages. First, you can centrally manage event collection across your organization directly from CloudWatch console without having to configure individual trails, reducing operational overhead.

note: Release date of this integration not found in the saved What's New pages; the FAQ gives no date.

claim: CloudTrail records API calls made from any client. The AWS Management Console, AWS SDKs, command line tools, and higher-level AWS services call AWS API operations, so these calls are recorded.
question: Are API calls made from the AWS Management Console recorded?

values.display: records API calls made from any client
command line tools

evidence.quote: CloudTrail records API calls made from any client. The AWS Management Console, AWS SDKs, command line tools, and higher-level AWS services call AWS API operations, so these calls are recorded.

claim: A trail that applies to all AWS Regions records AWS account activity across all Regions in which your data is stored. This setting also applies to any new Regions added.
question: What does it mean to apply a trail to all AWS Regions?

values.display: across all Regions
applies to any new Regions added

evidence.quote: Applying a trail to all AWS Regions refers to creating a trail that will record AWS account activity across all Regions in which your data is stored. This setting also applies to any new Regions added.

claim: When you apply a trail in all Regions, CloudTrail creates a new trail in each Region by replicating the trail configuration. It delivers log files with account activity across all Regions to a single S3 bucket and a single CloudWatch Logs log group.
question: What happens when I apply a trail to all Regions?

values.display: replicating the trail configuration
single S3 bucket and a single CloudWatch Logs log group

evidence.quote: Once you apply a trail in all Regions, CloudTrail will create a new trail by replicating the trail configuration. CloudTrail will record and process the log files in each Region and deliver log files containing account activity across all Regions to a single S3 bucket and a single CloudWatch Logs log group.

claim: If you specified an optional SNS topic for a trail applied to all Regions, CloudTrail delivers SNS notifications for all log files delivered to a single SNS topic.
question: Where do SNS notifications go for a trail that applies to all Regions?

values.display: optional Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic
a single SNS topic

evidence.quote: If you specified an optional Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic, CloudTrail will deliver Amazon SNS notifications for all log files delivered to a single SNS topic.

claim: You can create up to five trails in a Region. A trail that applies to all Regions exists in each Region and counts as one trail in each Region.
question: How many trails can I create in a Region?

values.display: up to five trails in a Region
counted as one trail in each Region

qualifiers.condition: The FAQ does not say whether the limit can be raised; see the CloudTrail quota page.

evidence.quote: You can create up to five trails in a Region. A trail that applies to all Regions exists in each Region and is counted as one trail in each Region.

claim: By default, CloudTrail log files are encrypted using S3 server-side encryption (SSE) and placed into your S3 bucket. You can control access to log files by applying IAM or S3 bucket policies.
question: How can I secure my CloudTrail log files?

values.display: encrypted using S3 server-side encryption (SSE)
IAM or S3 bucket policies

evidence.quote: By default, CloudTrail log files are encrypted using S3 server-side encryption (SSE) and placed into your S3 bucket. You can control access to log files by applying IAM or S3 bucket policies.

claim: You can add an additional layer of security for CloudTrail log files by enabling S3 multi-factor authentication (MFA) Delete on your S3 bucket.
question: How can I add another layer of protection for CloudTrail log files?

values.display: S3 multi-factor authentication (MFA) Delete
additional layer of security

evidence.quote: You can add an additional layer of security by enabling S3 multi-factor authentication (MFA) Delete on your S3 bucket.

claim: You control the retention policies for your CloudTrail log files. By default, log files are stored indefinitely. You can use S3 Object lifecycle management rules to define your own retention policy.
question: How long can I store my CloudTrail activity log files?

values.display: By default, log files are stored indefinitely
S3 Object lifecycle management rules

evidence.quote: You control the retention policies for your CloudTrail log files. By default, log files are stored indefinitely. You can use S3 Object lifecycle management rules to define your own retention policy.

claim: CloudTrail delivers log files to your S3 bucket approximately every five minutes. It does not deliver log files if no API calls are made on your account.

values.display: approximately every five minutes
does not deliver log files

evidence.quote: CloudTrail delivers log files to your S3 bucket approximately every five minutes. CloudTrail does not deliver log files if no API calls are made on your account.

claim: CloudTrail is designed to support at least one delivery of subscribed events to customer S3 buckets. In some situations, CloudTrail could deliver the same event more than once, so customers may notice duplicated events.
question: Is it possible to receive duplicate events?

values.display: at least one delivery of subscribed events
deliver the same event more than once

evidence.quote: CloudTrail is designed to support at least one delivery of subscribed events to customer S3 buckets. In some situations, it is possible that CloudTrail could deliver the same event more than once. As a result, customers may notice duplicated events.
